solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tours regularly around Naples, originally coming from Florence?

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals from the word Tours keeps the first, third and fifth

parts.note: CA, short for circa, is Latin for around

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word Naples

explanation.surface: A trip round Italian cities, starting at Naples and ending up in Florence.
explanation.definitionFit: Florence is the capital of Tuscany, so someone or something from there is Tuscan; the question mark flags definition by example.

clue.text: Carry out a couple of poles to plant in piece of land

indicators.note: to plant in means the pieces are set inside the word for land

parts.note: a tract is an area of land
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Putting a pair of posts into the ground on a plot.
explanation.definitionFit: To transact business is to conduct or carry it out.

clue.text: Maid watchful when old bachelor goes missing

indicators.note: goes missing means the letters for old bachelor are removed

parts.note: observant means watchful
O for old and B for bachelor

explanation.surface: A sharp-eyed housemaid notices when an elderly single man disappears.
explanation.definitionFit: A maid is a female domestic servant, so the general term covers her.

clue.text: Prosperity supplies a barrier to restrict disease

indicators.note: to restrict means the fence closes round the illness, holding it in

parts.note: a fence is a barrier
flu, influenza, is a disease

explanation.surface: Wealth pays for a barrier to contain an epidemic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supplies' is a link word: the wordplay supplies the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Affluence is wealth and abundance, which is what prosperity means.

clue.text: One on a dash, nothing to prevent covering over a mile

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

indicators.note: covering means the word for prevent wraps round the next pieces

parts.note: to prevent is to deter
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Something on a car's dashboard, with nothing stopping it from clocking over a mile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' puts OM inside DETER. The dash is the dashboard of a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A mileage counter sits on a car's dashboard, so it is one instrument found there.

clue.text: People following rich individual coming in today, moving fast

indicators.note: coming in means the rich person and the people enter the scrambled word
moving suggests the letters of today are shifted into a new order
following places the people after the rich individual

parts.note: a fat one, fat meaning rich
men are people

explanation.surface: A crowd trails a wealthy man arriving today, hurrying along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges the letters of today, and 'coming in' puts the rich one plus people inside. 'fast' looks like speed but is the noun for a period without food.
explanation.definitionFit: Yom Kippur, the Day of Atonement, is the holiest Jewish day, observed by abstaining from food and drink.

clue.text: Engine's temperature fell all round

indicators.note: all round means the moor surrounds the temperature letter

parts.note: a fell is a hill or moor in northern England

explanation.surface: The engine's heat dropped everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' looks like a verb but is the northern English noun for upland moor.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor is a machine producing motion, an engine.

clue.text: Ground where reptile doesn't keep quiet

indicators.note: doesn't keep means the letter for quiet is let go from the reptile's name

parts.note: a terrapin is a freshwater turtle, a reptile
P, piano, means quiet in music

explanation.surface: A place where a noisy reptile can't stay silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is land or ground considered in terms of its physical features.

clue.text: Employer turned up yours truly's CV

indicators.note: turned up, in a down clue, means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a user is one who employs something
yours truly is a jokey way of saying me

explanation.surface: A boss arrived holding my CV.
explanation.definitionFit: A résumé is the American term for a summary of one's career, a curriculum vitae.

clue.text: Author prepared to admit claim to be of high standard?

indicators.note: to admit means letting the boast in inside the word for prepared

parts.note: willing means prepared or ready

parts.words: claim to be of high standard
parts.note: I am gold is a boast of being top quality

explanation.surface: A writer ready to concede he claims to be first-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: William Golding wrote Lord of the Flies and won the Nobel Prize in Literature.

clue.text: Publicise, year upon year, entertainment of a delicate nature

parts.note: to air something is to make it public
a fair is an outdoor entertainment with rides and stalls
Y again abbreviates year

explanation.surface: Advertising a delicate show, repeated year after year.
explanation.definitionFit: Airy-fairy describes something flimsy and insubstantial, delicately vague in nature.

clue.text: Ring America after the peak

indicators.note: after places the abbreviation for America behind the word for a peak

parts.note: a tor is a rocky peak or hill, as on Dartmoor
US is short for the United States, America

explanation.surface: Phoning America once you have climbed the summit.
explanation.definitionFit: A torus is the doughnut-shaped geometric figure, a solid ring.

clue.text: Bird made of silver unwanted at first in auction

indicators.note: in places the silver and the initial letter inside the word for auction

parts.note: to sell, as at an auction
AG is the chemical symbol for silver, from Latin argentum

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the word unwanted

explanation.surface: A bird ornament made of silver that nobody wanted, sitting in a sale.
explanation.definitionFit: The seagull is a common seabird, so it is one example of a bird.

clue.text: Part of body shape swollen by organ

indicators.note: swollen by means the word for shape is filled out with the organ placed inside it

parts.note: form means shape
the ear is an organ of hearing

explanation.surface: A part of the body whose shape has puffed up because of some organ.
explanation.definitionFit: The forearm is the section of the arm between elbow and wrist, a bodily part.

clue.text: Risk a car crash, when two metals collide?

definitions.meaning: to swerve in front of another vehicle, risking a collision
copper, symbol CU, run into tin gives the letters side by side

explanation.surface: A driver taking risks on the road, framed as a collision between metals.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a pun: CU (copper) bumping into TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut in is to pull sharply in front of another vehicle, a manoeuvre that courts a collision.

clue.text: Against coins not using English metal? Sort of

parts.note: anti means against

indicators.note: not using means the letter for English is dropped from the word for coins

parts.note: coins are money

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to coins, refusing English ones, asks about a metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' hedges the definition: the element is a metalloid, only partly a metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Antimony is a brittle metalloid, sharing properties with metals without being a true one.

clue.text: Solid surface, one on a nut

parts.note: macadam is the compacted broken-stone road surface
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A hard surface with one nut sitting on it.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'one on a' puts I above A.
explanation.definitionFit: The macadamia is an Australian tree whose round edible seed is a popular nut.

clue.text: Sport's over: fits horribly and dies

indicators.note: over means the word is turned over and read backwards

parts.note: sport is fun, and the possessive gives FUNS

indicators.note: horribly signals that the letters of fits are mangled into another order

explanation.surface: The game has ended: someone has awful seizures and dies.
explanation.definitionFit: To snuff it is a slang idiom for to die.

clue.text: Mercenary ruing he'd fired

indicators.note: fired suggests the letters are shot off and land in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A soldier for pay regretting the shot he let off.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired gun is a person paid to fight or kill, a mercenary.

clue.text: Isn't an awfully short time? It is

definitions.text: Isn't an awfully short time? It is

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters of the words are badly jumbled

parts.note: T is the short form, abbreviation, for time

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question answered by itself: surely that's a very brief moment? Yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges the letters of isn't an, and T for time follows; the whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An instant is a moment, the briefest span of time.

clue.text: Cold store for wine with a hidden compartment

indicators.note: hidden means the letter a is tucked away inside the other pieces

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a bin is a rack or store for wine bottles

explanation.surface: A cool wine store that has a secret compartment.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabin is a private room on a ship or a section of an aircraft, an enclosed compartment.

clue.text: One line crossed by old farmers, tough old birds

indicators.note: crossed by means the old farmers stretch across and enclose the other pieces

parts.note: the Boers were Dutch settler farmers in South Africa; boer is Dutch for farmer
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A single line of old farmers raising hardy elderly chickens.
explanation.definitionFit: Boilers are old hens too tough for roasting, only fit to boil.

clue.text: Fabric cut: it is seen in a soft glow

indicators.note: cut means the fabric's word loses its final letter

parts.note: twill is a woven fabric with diagonal ribs

explanation.surface: Cutting cloth under gentle lamplight.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilit means lit by twilight, the dim soft light after sunset.

clue.text: Complain pathetically about idiot revelry

indicators.note: about means the word for complaining goes round the word for idiot

parts.note: to wail is to lament or complain piteously
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Someone whining feebly about a fool's partying.
explanation.definitionFit: Wassail is old festive drinking and merrymaking, hence revelry.

clue.text: A niqab is said to be useful

indicators.note: is said signals that the words sound like the answer when spoken

parts.note: a niqab is a veil covering the face, so a niqab is a veil

explanation.surface: A claim that a face covering serves a practical purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: To avail is to be of use or help, as in 'nothing availed'.

clue.text: Stomach feeble returning musical phrase

indicators.note: returning means the word for feeble is read backwards

parts.note: dim can mean feeble or faint
a riff is a short repeated musical phrase

explanation.surface: A weak gut feeling coming back with a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: The midriff is the middle front of the body, the area of the stomach.

clue.text: In American city, possesses capital

indicators.note: In places the word for possesses inside the abbreviation for the city

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
has means possesses

explanation.surface: In a US city, someone owns a lot of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Lhasa is the capital city of Tibet.

clue.text: Hotels cover the earth profusely

indicators.note: cover means the word for hotels wraps round the earth pigment

parts.note: inns are hotels
umber is a brown earth used as a pigment

explanation.surface: A chain of hotels spreads over the whole planet in great quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving in numbers means arriving in great quantity, so the phrase means abundantly.

clue.text: Say, a call in court is rejected by union instruction

indicators.note: by puts the union abbreviation alongside, ahead of the turned pieces

parts.note: TU is short for trade union

indicators.note: is rejected means the run of pieces is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: EG, for example, is signalled by say
let is the umpire's call on a tennis court when a serve clips the net

explanation.surface: A legal summons is turned down because a trade union says so.
explanation.walkthrough: The court is a tennis court, not a law court; 'is rejected' turns EGALET into TELAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutelage is teaching or guidance, so it means instruction.

clue.text: Team of lawyers in literary county

parts.note: the Bar is the collective body of barristers
a set is a group or team

explanation.surface: A group of barristers working in a county known from books.
explanation.walkthrough: BARSET is the fictional English county of Anthony Trollope's Barsetshire novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Barset is the invented shire of Trollope's novels, a county existing only in fiction.
